newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran rejects U.S. charges on Chinese chemical arms.
newsitem.headline: Iran rejects U.S. charges on Chinese chemical arms.

text.p: Iran dismissed U.S. charges that Chinese firms had transfered chemical weapons technology to Tehran as "thoroughly fabricated", the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Saturday.

It quoted Kamal Kharrazi, Iran's ambassador to the United Nations, as slamming Washington's decision to impose sanctions on several Chinese entities for at least a year for allegedly transferring chemical weapons components to Tehran.

"Washington has once again resorted to baseless claims in an irresponsible manner in connection with the peaceful activities of the Iranian chemical industries," IRNA quoted him as saying late on Friday.

U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright told a Senate committee on Thursday there was no evidence the Chinese government was involved in the transfers, which she said involved chemicals and other technology that could be used in chemical weapons.
The sanctions affected two Chinese firms and five citizens.
China condemned the U.S. sanctions as "unreasonable" and said it was firmly opposed to penalties.

Kharrazi said: "Such statements, like similar cases in the past, are aimed at depriving the Islamic Republic of the legal right to expand its chemical industries for non-military purposes in accordance with articles of the chemical weapons treaty."

"The Islamic Republic, as a signatory to the treaty on non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and a victim of these weapons during the Iraqi-imposed war, rejects all allegations of any plan to produce chemical weapons in Iran," Kharrazi said. He was referring to the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.
